MODULE: MarketWatch Resource Map | v0.01d | build 040 | 8 Oct 2026 EDT | fn: rmRender(), rmApply(), rmMeasure()

MarketWatch resource map — heaviest first

Mode: DEFAULT - metals + dividends data OFF and their tests paused (tick them + Apply to turn on)
  • Biggest win: uncheck TF_STORE (4.8 MB timeframe cache) — 70% of the file, ~9 MB less heap, no errors in tests.
  • Safe to split (tested): TF_STORE, _METALS, WB_PRELOAD, _UB, _DIVDATA — replaced by empty structures; app loads, all 412 buttons present, 70 button clicks gave 0 errors. Features that read that data show empty until data is fetched live.
  • Keep for now: app code snapshot, SEEDS, the 4,900-node page and its 56 timers — not separable without risk (untested).
  • Metals + dividends: OFF by default (data and tests). Turn them on only by ticking their Keep box and pressing Apply. Earlier note: MarketWatch now always loads with its metals test and dividend test PAUSED (they only run when you resume them in the bottom bar or press the Run metals button inside MarketWatch).
  • Suggested: phone/tablet or low RAM → LITE; laptop → LITE + tick back only what you need; 55" / desktop → FULL. Pick parts, then press Apply (reloads MarketWatch only if open).
Suggestions
  1. Light copy in the app panel, full copy in the browser: keep this panel as the lightweight companion (no MarketWatch loaded). Open the link in a Chrome/Firefox tab and press Float MarketWatch there, where there is more RAM and screen room.
  2. Download the full app once: use the green MarketWatch / SANDBOX .html export buttons, then open that downloaded file straight from your folder in a browser tab. That runs the full 6.7 MB app locally with no extra sandbox load.
  3. Do not run both heavy copies in the same window: two MarketWatch copies at once double the memory and CPU. Use the app panel for the companion and the browser tab for MarketWatch.
  4. Storage is separate: the desktop app and each browser keep their own saved slots and settings, so they will not sync with each other. Use the download buttons to move data between them.
  5. Live data: Webull bars only flow where the artifact runs inside Claude (app or claude.ai). A downloaded file opened offline can show the app, but not the companion's live Webull feed.
Pulls live crypto bars through your Webull connector and runs light backtests. Research only, not advice; past results do not predict future ones.

MODULE: Resource Meter + Mode Ladder | v0.01d | build 039 | fn: res()

Resource use and how to keep every function available

ModeLoadsMemoryBacktestHistory download
Lite (default)companion + stills only~15-30 MB8 variants x 4 symbols x 300 bars (about 50 ms)CSV / TXT / small JSON through the download button
Standard+ control deck on demand, one app copy~150-300 MB+ forward tests, queued one at a time+ history preload (402 KB) and per-symbol files
FullMarketWatch raw / float, in a browser tab400 MB+everything, run in idle slicesfull 4.7 MB JSON / 8.2 MB CSV, streamed
  1. Time: run backtests in slices of about 12 ms (setTimeout / requestIdleCallback) or a Web Worker so the page never freezes; one heavy job at a time in a queue; skip runs when the tab is hidden.
  2. Memory: never load two MarketWatch copies; unload the iframe when hidden; keep bars as typed arrays; cap live history at the newest 300 bars per symbol.
  3. Cache: cache backtest results by symbol + timeframe + last-bar time, so unchanged bars are not recomputed; cache history files with the Cache API under a version key and keep at most 3 backups of the same version; put big data in IndexedDB, not localStorage (about 5 MB limit).
  4. CPU: refetch about every 60 s only while visible; back off to 5 min on battery or when long tasks pile up; heavy variants (Donchian, SMA+RSI) can be skipped first in Lite.
  5. History download: fetch as a blob (no text decoding), split the big export per symbol (4 files of about 2 MB), optionally gzip with CompressionStream, and resume from the last timestamp so a failed run does not restart.
  6. Storage: the meter above shows quota use; over 80 percent it warns before saving, and the oldest of the 3 backups is dropped first.
MODULE: History Download Catalog (by symbol) | v0.01d | build 040 | 8 Oct 2026 EDT | fn: render(), build(), dl()

History downloads — every symbol, timeframe and date range

Earliest Latest Newest bars per series
Timeframes (none picked = all):
Not loaded. The catalog reads the MarketWatch file once, lists every series, and frees the memory after 3 idle minutes.
How it works: each row is one symbol; the pills are its timeframes with row counts (hover for the date range; click a pill to exclude it). Row buttons download that symbol only; tick several symbols for a grouped download; group buttons download a whole source. Earliest / Latest / Newest-N / timeframe filters apply to every download. Columns: source, symbol, timeframe, timestamp_ms, time_utc, open, high, low, close, dividend (dividend bars: open + close only; metals XAU/XAG: closes only). Weekly and monthly series are separate rows, not computed from daily.

Linked pages & data (load separately)

Each item is its own file next to this page and only downloads when opened (previews of the two apps load when scrolled into view). Opens in a new tab.
